solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reduced force includes soldiers on board of the highest quality

indicators.note: the shortened word holds another inside it, as a box includes its contents
something reduced has been cut short, so the word for force loses its final letter

parts.note: to prise is to force something open with leverage
marines are soldiers who serve aboard ship

explanation.surface: A weakened military force somehow still contains the finest troops serving on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced force' reads like a smaller army, but force here is a verb for levering something open.
explanation.definitionFit: Primariness is the noun for being primary, that is first in rank or excellence.

clue.text: Mediator clear on study dominated by ministers

parts.note: a priest mediates between people and God
to rid is to clear of something
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A go-between clears up after studying, while dominated by ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first pieces above the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Priest-ridden describes a place unduly controlled by clergy, ministers of religion.

clue.text: Onion recipe for colt in training school

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter stands in where another was

parts.note: a camp, as in a boot camp or training camp
C is the racing abbreviation for colt
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction for a young horse at a riding school, absurdly calling for onion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe for colt' swaps R in where C stood in CAMP. A ramp is a wild onion (ramsons), a Chambers word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramps are wild garlic or broad-leaved leeks, plants of the onion family.

clue.text: Rocky with cast sinks wine being drunk

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaky, so the letters wobble into a new arrangement
cast here means thrown away, so the named letter is discarded from the pool

explanation.surface: A shaky person, along with the plaster cast, sinks wine and gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with cast' throws W out of SINKS WINE; 'Rocky' rearranges the rest. 'Inky' is Australian slang for drunk, so the answer is the state of being so.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky is Australian slang for intoxicated, so the noun names the condition of being intoxicated.

clue.text: Jerk taking money for hotel to play hookey

indicators.note: taking means accepting one thing into the word on offer
for means in place of, so the money letter stands where the hotel letter was

parts.note: a hitch is a sudden jerk or tug
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lout takes cash for a hotel room rather than going to school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking money for hotel': M comes in 'for' the H at the start of HITCH. To mitch is dialect for to play truant.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitch is an old dialect verb for skipping school, the same as playing truant.

clue.text: Run over the best possible dream

indicators.note: in a down entry over means placed above, so the first piece sits on top

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
every can mean all possible, as in every chance of success

explanation.surface: Running over the ideal outcome in a daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: Revery is a variant spelling of reverie, a daydream.

clue.text: Spooner's offering place that's knotty

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening consonant sounds, as the Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: an offering is a donation, said aloud as two sounds, 'doh' and 'nation'; the first is spelt DO and the second NATION
the rest of the same spoken word for offering, after its opening 'doh', is spelt NATION

explanation.surface: A gift to the church from the famous slip-prone Oxford don, tied in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' swaps opening sounds; here the swap is inside the one word for offering, 'do-nation', whose D and N change places to give 'no-dation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodation is a rare Chambers word for a knotted place or the forming of knots.

clue.text: Due to be renovated, technology college and English school

indicators.note: renovated means made over afresh, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
CAT was a College of Advanced Technology in Britain
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A technical college and an English school are due for refurbishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun in this setting but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them, so the verb means to educate.

clue.text: Last in party to leave, Guy and Heather going

indicators.note: the chosen letter departs from the next word, removing it

parts.note: a guy is a rope stay supporting a tent or mast

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of party
ling is common heather

explanation.surface: The last party guest leaves, with Guy and Heather heading off too.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy and Heather look like names but are a rope and a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To stale is to urinate, of horses and cattle, so staling is going in the informal sense.

clue.text: Fighting people ring about entering office after one

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within another
after places the office part later, following the earlier pieces

parts.note: to ring is to sound a bell
I is the Roman numeral one
office can mean a lavatory, and the gents is a men's lavatory
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A boxing ring scrap spills into the office after one combatant arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: In Chambers 'office' can mean a lavatory; in British usage the gents is the men's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerents are the nations or parties engaged in a war or fight.

clue.text: Nicked close to windpipe on part of tongue

parts.note: ran in is slang for arrested, as nicked is

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of windpipe

explanation.surface: Someone or something was cut near the windpipe, landing on the tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes 'on': RANINE means relating to the underside of the tongue, as in the ranine artery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranine is an anatomical adjective for the region beneath the tongue, where a frog-shaped swelling can form.

clue.text: Cheer a lot of old-fashioned salt

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: io is a Greek cry of joy or triumph
dated means out of fashion

explanation.surface: A toast with plenty of some antiquated seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: An iodate is a chemical salt of iodic acid, so salt names the class it belongs to.

clue.text: Terribly loud vicar right apart on the Tube

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly messed up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
set apart means taken away, so the abbreviation for right is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A noisy clergyman stands apart from the crowd on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tube' looks like the London Underground; here it is the oviduct, the tube carrying eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviducal is the adjective for the oviduct, the egg-carrying tube in the body.

clue.text: Nice grocer's impressive with timeless range

indicators.note: less means without, so the abbreviation for time is taken out of the following word

parts.note: epic means grand and impressive
a tier is a row or rank, a range of seats

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is praised for an impressive range of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, so the grocer is a French word; T for time leaves TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicier is French for grocer, so a grocer in Nice would be called one.

clue.text: Blackbird not unknown in Scottish island

indicators.note: not means without here, so the letter for an unknown is struck out

parts.note: colly is an old name for the blackbird, as in colly birds
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A blackbird that is no stranger to a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Coll is an island of the Inner Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Lady in Lisbon Sheraton out to entrap leader of industry

indicators.note: to entrap is to hold something caught inside
out suggests disorder, so the hotel name is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of industry

explanation.surface: A woman in Lisbon goes out from her hotel to snare a captain of industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged hotel name traps I between R and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Senhorita is the Portuguese title for an unmarried woman, as used in Lisbon.

clue.text: Spotted criminal unit in short western

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
short means cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an oater is a western film
a cell is a small group in a criminal or terrorist network

explanation.surface: A gang has been seen in a cut-down cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: An oater is American slang for a western, from the horses eating oats.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocellate means marked with eye-like spots, as on a peacock's tail.

clue.text: Derision shown by audience rapping three old actors

indicators.note: read as wrapping, one word is folded round the other

parts.note: an audience hisses to show contempt
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: An audience jeers as three performers attempt rap.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural here is old-fashioned, hence 'old actors'.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrio is an archaic word for a stage player, from Latin histrio, actor.

clue.text: Jumper lifted up in error is clumsy

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside another

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake

indicators.note: lifted up in a down entry means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

explanation.surface: Pulling a sweater on upside down by mistake looks gauche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is a sweater in British English, but here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Boorish means rude and uncouth, clumsy in manners.

clue.text: Indian city is involved in obscure scheme

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within, so one piece is placed inside

parts.note: dim means obscure or faint
Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: An Indian city gets caught up in a murky plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme can be a plan or outline drawing, which is what a diagram is.

clue.text: Veteran's writing till money comes in

indicators.note: one word comes in, entering the other and sitting inside it

parts.note: to till the soil is to dig it
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: An old soldier writes until his pay arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veteran's' marks an archaic word: Spenser's dite means compose, so diting is writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Diting is an obsolete word for composing or writing, so an old word for writing.

clue.text: More promising runs with Boycott opening

indicators.note: opening puts the name first, at the start, before the other piece

parts.note: Rosie Boycott is a British journalist and newspaper editor
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Runs pile up with Geoffrey Boycott, the Yorkshire opening batsman, at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture wants Geoffrey Boycott; it is the journalist Rosie Boycott whose first name is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosy outlook is a hopeful one, so rosier prospects are more promising ones.

clue.text: Man in tangle gets engaged

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a mess is a tangle or muddle
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man in a muddle gets betrothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' suggests marriage, but it is gears interlocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear wheels mesh when their teeth interlock, which is to engage.

clue.text: Rationale designed for person prone to distancing?

indicators.note: designed means made up or reworked to a plan, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reasoned justification drawn up for someone who keeps others at arm's length.
explanation.definitionFit: An alienator estranges people, pushing them away, which the question mark frames as distancing.

clue.text: Ignore my amatory larking, it does come from the heart

definitions.text: it does come from the heart

indicators.note: ignore tells us to leave the named letters out of the pool
larking means playing about, so the remaining letters frolic into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells a partner to disregard their flirtatious play, but insists it is heartfelt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignore my' drops M and Y from AMATORY, leaving AATOR, which 'larking' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the great artery carrying blood away from the left ventricle.

clue.text: Trace a 1986 vehicle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tiny residue or remnant
second meaning: a car with a UK registration plate whose year letter was D, issued 1986 to 1987

explanation.walkthrough: UK number plates once began with a year letter; D was used for cars registered in 1986-87, so such a car was a D-reg.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreg is a small leftover quantity, while D-reg is British shorthand for a car registered with year letter D.

clue.text: Playwright from large Pacific island dropping round

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, a clothing size

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of, so one ring-shaped letter is lost

parts.note: Borneo is a large island in the western Pacific region
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A dramatist hails from a big island in the Pacific, minus a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large' already gave OS, so 'large Pacific island' should not be read as one thing.
explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne was the English dramatist who wrote Look Back in Anger.

clue.text: Japanese food thrown up in club

indicators.note: thrown up in a down entry means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Japanese food is vomited at a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Nori is dried seaweed used in Japanese cooking to wrap sushi.

clue.text: Character with identity remitted hot money, cash used in Argos?

indicators.note: remitted read as sent back, so the first two pieces run backwards

parts.note: a card is an eccentric character
ID is short for identity
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: Someone sends cash with ID, asking whether it can be spent at the high-street shop Argos.
explanation.walkthrough: Argos is a British catalogue store chain, but here it is the ancient Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: A didrachm was an ancient Greek silver coin worth two drachmas, current in cities like Argos.

clue.text: Close chum starts to surrender all possessions

indicators.note: starts means the first letters of each word, and surrender means they are given up

parts.note: a close chum is a best mate

explanation.surface: A dear friend begins to give up everything they own.
explanation.walkthrough: BEST MATE loses its two initials, B and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is the whole of their property and assets, especially at death.

clue.text: Squeeze former partner, tense by the sound of it

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: we hear rather than see the word, so its sound is used and spelt differently

parts.note: taut means tense, and in non-rhotic speech it is said like tort

explanation.surface: Someone puts pressure on an ex, which sounds a tense business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeeze' also suggests a partner, as in main squeeze, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeeze someone for money is to extort it from them by pressure or threats.

clue.text: Tendency to get equilibrium in secret police, nothing succeeded externally

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: externally means on the outside, so these letters surround the next piece

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
the Stasi were the East German secret police

explanation.surface: A policy of balance among the old East German secret police, while nothing went on outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link here: it means at home. 'externally' puts nothing and succeeded around the old East German secret police.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeostasis is a system's tendency to keep a stable internal balance.
